labels.user-setting: user setting: users can change it

settings.title: Profile name
settings.description: The profile's name. A policy map refers to profiles by this name, and it becomes the file name of the compiled output. Letters, numbers, underscores and hyphens only.

settings.title: Description
settings.description: A note for people reading the file. It isn't written to any tool.

macos.note: For people reading the profile only.

linux.note: For people reading the profile only.

windows.note: For people reading the profile only.

macos.note: For people reading the profile only.

linux.note: For people reading the profile only.

windows.note: For people reading the profile only.

macos.note: For people reading the profile only.

linux.note: For people reading the profile only.

windows.note: For people reading the profile only.

settings.title: Allowed sandbox modes
settings.description: Which Codex sandbox modes users may pick. Leaving out danger-full-access stops Codex from running commands with no sandbox. A list with only read-only makes this a read-only profile, which only Codex can enforce.

macos.note: Not written. A read-only-only list stops the profile compiling for Claude.

linux.note: Not written. A read-only-only list stops the profile compiling for Claude.

windows.note: Not written. A read-only-only list stops the profile compiling for Claude.

macos.note: Not written. A read-only-only list stops the profile compiling for OpenCode.

linux.note: Not written. A read-only-only list stops the profile compiling for OpenCode.

windows.note: Not written. A read-only-only list stops the profile compiling for OpenCode.

settings.title: Default permission profile
settings.description: The permission profile Codex starts with: a built-in one such as :workspace or :read-only, or one you define under Permission profiles. If that profile turns command networking off, Claude and OpenCode block network access as well as they can.

macos.note: Only network.enabled: false is used. With claude.sandbox: required the OS sandbox blocks shell networking; otherwise curl, wget, ssh and scp are denied.

linux.note: Only network.enabled: false is used. With claude.sandbox: required the OS sandbox blocks shell networking; otherwise curl, wget, ssh and scp are denied.

windows.note: Only network.enabled: false is used. Claude has no OS sandbox on Windows, so only curl, wget, ssh and scp are denied.

macos.note: Only network.enabled: false is used, which denies OpenCode's web fetch tool. :read-only isn't supported.

linux.note: Only network.enabled: false is used, which denies OpenCode's web fetch tool. :read-only isn't supported.

windows.note: Only network.enabled: false is used, which denies OpenCode's web fetch tool. :read-only isn't supported.

settings.title: Allowed permission profiles
settings.description: Which permission profiles users may switch to in Codex. Set a profile to true to allow it.

settings.title: Permission profiles
settings.description: Named Codex permission profiles: what commands may read and write on disk, and whether they get network access. Codex enforces them in its OS sandbox. Claude and OpenCode can't, so a profile with filesystem rules or extends: :read-only stops the file compiling for them.

macos.note: Filesystem rules and :read-only aren't supported. network.enabled: false is used only on the default profile.

linux.note: Filesystem rules and :read-only aren't supported. network.enabled: false is used only on the default profile.

windows.note: Filesystem rules and :read-only aren't supported. network.enabled: false is used only on the default profile.

macos.note: Filesystem rules and :read-only aren't supported. network.enabled: false is used only on the default profile.

linux.note: Filesystem rules and :read-only aren't supported. network.enabled: false is used only on the default profile.

windows.note: Filesystem rules and :read-only aren't supported. network.enabled: false is used only on the default profile.

settings.title: Windows sandbox types
settings.description: Which of Codex's Windows sandbox types users may run. elevated isolates network access better than unelevated. This doesn't control Codex's newer MXC sandbox; see Allow the MXC sandbox.

macos.note: Windows only.

linux.note: Windows only.

settings.title: Allow the MXC sandbox
settings.description: Set to false to stop Codex using Microsoft's MXC sandbox on Windows, whether Codex picks it automatically or a user chooses it. The Windows sandbox types setting still applies.

macos.note: Windows only.

linux.note: Windows only.

settings.title: Claude OS sandbox
settings.description: Whether Claude must run shell commands in its OS sandbox. required turns the sandbox on and stops Claude starting without it, so blocked files and network stay blocked even in shell commands. tools-only accepts that those settings apply only to Claude's own tools. A profile with blocked files or networking off must choose. unix covers macOS and Linux.

macos.note: The sandbox is built in.

linux.note: Needs bubblewrap and socat installed; with required, Claude won't start without them.

windows.note: No Claude sandbox on native Windows: use tools-only.

settings.title: Allowed approval policies
settings.description: When Codex must stop and ask before acting. Users can only pick from this list.

settings.title: Allowed approval reviewers
settings.description: Who may answer Codex's approval requests: the person (user) or Codex's automatic reviewer (auto_review).

settings.title: Bypass mode
settings.description: Whether users may skip approvals. AgentEdict checks this only in read-only profiles, which must say forbidden; it isn't written to any file. Claude's bypass mode is always turned off.

macos.note: Checked for read-only profiles only; not written.

linux.note: Checked for read-only profiles only; not written.

windows.note: Checked for read-only profiles only; not written.

settings.title: Approval reviewer guidance
settings.description: Extra guidance for Codex's automatic approval reviewer: what to approve and what to deny. Claude and OpenCode receive the same text as instructions. It guides the model; it doesn't block anything on its own.

settings.title: Blocked files
settings.description: Paths the agent must never read, such as SSH keys and cloud credentials. common applies everywhere; unix covers macOS and Linux. OpenCode can't block reads, so a profile with this setting doesn't compile for OpenCode.

macos.note: Shell commands are blocked only with claude.sandbox: required; with tools-only, only Claude's file tools are.

linux.note: Shell commands are blocked only with claude.sandbox: required; with tools-only, only Claude's file tools are.

windows.note: Claude's file tools only. Shell commands can still read these paths on Windows.

macos.note: OpenCode can't block reads. The profile won't compile for OpenCode.

linux.note: OpenCode can't block reads. The profile won't compile for OpenCode.

windows.note: OpenCode can't block reads. The profile won't compile for OpenCode.

settings.title: Deny commands
settings.description: Commands the agent may never run, matched by how the command starts: "sudo" blocks every sudo command. common applies everywhere; unix covers macOS and Linux.

macos.note: Matched by Claude's permission rules.

linux.note: Matched by Claude's permission rules.

windows.note: Matched by Claude's permission rules.

settings.title: Ask before commands
settings.description: Commands the agent must ask about before running, matched by how the command starts.

settings.title: Allow commands
settings.description: Commands the agent may run without asking, matched by how the command starts. Codex has no allow rules in its admin file; its approval policy decides.

macos.note: Codex's admin file has no allow rules.

linux.note: Codex's admin file has no allow rules.

windows.note: Codex's admin file has no allow rules.

macos.note: Only these managed allow rules count; users' own rules are ignored.

linux.note: Only these managed allow rules count; users' own rules are ignored.

windows.note: Only these managed allow rules count; users' own rules are ignored.

settings.title: Allow login shells
settings.description: Whether Codex may start commands in a login shell, which loads the user's shell profile scripts.

settings.title: Web search
settings.description: Which kinds of web search the agent may use. disabled on its own turns web search off. OpenCode follows the first mode: disabled denies its web fetch tool, live allows it, anything else asks.

macos.note: Only the first mode is used.

linux.note: Only the first mode is used.

windows.note: Only the first mode is used.

settings.title: Browser use rules
settings.description: What Codex may do in a browser on any site: visiting, uploading, downloading and full browser control, each allow or deny, and whether a site approval lasts for one turn or the whole thread. Leave a choice unset to keep Codex's default.

settings.title: Codex app: allowed hosts

fields.label: Limit the app to these hosts

settings.description: Limits which hosts the Codex desktop app itself may contact, for example only your model gateway. Hosts not listed are blocked. Use exact host names such as gateway.example.com, without https://, a port or wildcards. It doesn't cover commands Codex runs or the processes they start; use Permission profiles for those.

settings.title: Computer use while locked
settings.description: Whether Codex may control the computer while the screen is locked.

settings.title: Allow browser and computer use
settings.description: Master switch for Codex controlling a browser or the computer.

settings.title: Allow Appshots
settings.description: Whether Codex may take screenshots of apps (Appshots).

settings.title: Allow remote control
settings.description: Whether a Codex session on this machine may be driven from another device.

settings.title: MCP servers

fields.label: Local server on macOS and Linux

settings.description: The only MCP servers the agent may use. Leave the list empty to allow none. Give each server a URL, or the command that starts it on each OS. The trust flag is accepted but not written to any tool yet.

macos.note: Matched by URL or launch command.

linux.note: Matched by URL or launch command.

windows.note: Matched by URL or launch command.

macos.note: Matched by server name only.

linux.note: Matched by server name only.

windows.note: Matched by server name only.

macos.note: Adds these servers; it doesn't stop users adding their own.

linux.note: Adds these servers; it doesn't stop users adding their own.

windows.note: Adds these servers; it doesn't stop users adding their own.

settings.title: Plugin MCP servers
settings.description: The MCP servers each Codex plugin may run, matched by URL or launch command. A plugin listed with no servers may run none, and an empty list allows no plugin servers at all. Give each server a URL or a command, not both.

settings.title: Apps
settings.description: Whether Codex may use connected apps. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: Browser use
settings.description: Whether Codex may control its built-in browser. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: External browser use
settings.description: Whether Codex may control a browser outside Codex. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: Full browser control
settings.description: Whether Codex may use full Chrome DevTools Protocol access to a browser. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: Computer use
settings.description: Whether Codex may control the mouse, keyboard and screen. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: In-app browser
settings.description: Whether Codex may open web pages in its in-app browser. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: Memories
settings.description: Whether Codex may remember things between sessions. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: Multiple agents
settings.description: Whether Codex may start helper agents. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: Plugin sharing
settings.description: Whether users may share Codex plugins. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: Plugins
settings.description: Whether Codex may use plugins. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: Remote plugins
settings.description: Whether Codex may install plugins from remote sources. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: Automatic approval reviewer
settings.description: Whether Codex's automatic reviewer may answer approval requests. Set to false to turn the feature off for everyone.

settings.title: Prefer the MXC sandbox
settings.description: Whether Codex runs Windows commands in Microsoft's newer MXC sandbox when the device supports it. Codex still falls back to the elevated or unelevated sandbox where MXC isn't available, so this can't require MXC. To block MXC, use Allow the MXC sandbox.

macos.note: Windows only.

linux.note: Windows only.

windows.note: Windows 11 24H2 or 25H2 with Microsoft's MXC capabilities. Falls back to the older sandboxes elsewhere.

settings.title: Sign-in methods
settings.description: How users may sign in to Codex: chatgpt (a ChatGPT account), api (an API key), or both. Codex reads this only from a local requirements.toml, not from the cloud console.

settings.title: Codex model for new threads
settings.description: Default Codex model for new threads. Requires model_provider. Explicit client model or reasoning overrides can replace this default; custom aliases need matching model catalog metadata.

settings.title: Model provider
settings.description: The model provider Codex must use, overriding what users and sessions choose: a built-in one such as openai, or one you define under Model providers.

settings.title: Model providers

fields.label: Environment variable with the API key

settings.description: Model providers Codex may use, such as a company gateway. Each replaces any provider with the same ID that users set up. Name the environment variable that holds the API key; never put the key itself in this file.

settings.title: Managed hooks only
settings.description: Whether Codex runs only hooks the administrator installed, ignoring hooks users add. AgentEdict writes true unless you say otherwise.

settings.title: Send feedback
settings.description: Whether users may send feedback reports to OpenAI from Codex.

settings.title: Instructions for the agent
settings.description: Text added to every conversation, such as "check authentication changes for security risks". It guides the model; it doesn't block anything.

settings.title: Telemetry export
settings.description: Sends Codex usage events to your OpenTelemetry collector. Only `edict compile` writes it, for Codex-only read-only profiles, as a separate <name>.codex.config.toml; bundles don't install it.

macos.note: Written only by edict compile for read-only profiles; not installed by bundles.

linux.note: Written only by edict compile for read-only profiles; not installed by bundles.

windows.note: Written only by edict compile for read-only profiles; not installed by bundles.

settings.title: Turn off auto-update
settings.description: Meant to stop agents updating themselves. AgentEdict accepts this field but doesn't write it to any tool yet.

macos.note: Accepted but not written yet.

linux.note: Accepted but not written yet.

windows.note: Accepted but not written yet.

macos.note: Accepted but not written yet.

linux.note: Accepted but not written yet.

windows.note: Accepted but not written yet.

macos.note: Accepted but not written yet.

linux.note: Accepted but not written yet.

windows.note: Accepted but not written yet.

settings.title: Native profile name
settings.description: The native profile's name. A policy map refers to it by this name. Letters, numbers, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or number.

settings.title: Gemini: default for unlisted tools
settings.description: What Gemini CLI does with a tool call no rule covers: deny it, or ask the user.

macos.note: Admin policy files override user and command-line tool rules.

linux.note: Admin policy files override user and command-line tool rules.

windows.note: Admin policy files override user and command-line tool rules.

settings.title: Gemini: tool rules
settings.description: Allow, deny or ask rules for Gemini CLI's tools, shell commands by prefix, and MCP servers. A higher priority wins; 950 is reserved. Denying MCP tools doesn't stop MCP servers starting.

settings.title: Gemini: turn off YOLO mode
settings.description: Stops users switching Gemini CLI into YOLO mode, which approves every tool call.

macos.note: The GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH variable can point Gemini at another settings file.

linux.note: The GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH variable can point Gemini at another settings file.

windows.note: The GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH variable can point Gemini at another settings file.

settings.title: Gemini: turn off "always allow"
settings.description: Stops users answering a prompt with "always allow".

macos.note: The GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH variable can point Gemini at another settings file.

linux.note: The GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH variable can point Gemini at another settings file.

windows.note: The GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH variable can point Gemini at another settings file.

settings.title: Gemini: default sandbox
settings.description: Which sandbox Gemini CLI uses by default. disabled, auto, docker and podman work everywhere; sandbox-exec is macOS only, runsc and lxc are Linux only, and windows-native is Windows only. Users can still change it.

macos.note: Also sandbox-exec.

linux.note: Also runsc and lxc.

windows.note: Also windows-native.

settings.title: Cursor: allowed tools, commands and MCP tools
settings.description: Cursor hooks that let only listed tools, exact shell commands and exact MCP tools run. Anything not listed is denied, so empty lists deny everything. It's a guardrail in Cursor's hooks, not an OS sandbox.

macos.note: Hook guardrail: Cursor starts hooks through the user's shell, so a changed shell environment can get around it.

linux.note: Hook guardrail: Cursor starts hooks through the user's shell, so a changed shell environment can get around it.

windows.note: Hook guardrail: Cursor starts hooks through the user's shell, so a changed shell environment can get around it.

settings.title: Antigravity: allowed tools, files, commands and sites
settings.description: An Antigravity hook that lets only listed tools, folders, exact commands and sites through. Anything else is denied, including MCP tools. Each user must turn the hook on, and can turn it off.

macos.note: Each user enrolls the hook and can disable it in settings.

linux.note: Each user enrolls the hook and can disable it in settings.

windows.note: Each user enrolls the hook and can disable it in settings.

settings.title: Copilot: turn off bypass mode
settings.description: Blocks --yolo, --allow-all and similar switches that skip Copilot's prompts. On by default.

macos.note: An open Copilot issue reports non-interactive -p sessions can still bypass it.

linux.note: An open Copilot issue reports non-interactive -p sessions can still bypass it.

windows.note: An open Copilot issue reports non-interactive -p sessions can still bypass it.

settings.title: Copilot: tool rules
settings.description: Allow, ask and deny rules such as Shell(git push *), Read(~/.ssh/**), Edit(//etc/**) or Domain(*.example.com). Deny beats ask, and ask beats allow. A rule can't be in two lists.

settings.title: Copilot: MCP servers

fields.label: Allowed servers (empty allows only built-in ones)

settings.description: Which MCP servers Copilot may use, matched by exact name, URL pattern or exact launch command. Deny wins. An empty allowed list blocks every server except built-in ones.

settings.title: Copilot: sandbox
settings.description: Turns on Copilot's own sandbox for commands. Needs Copilot CLI 1.0.93, VS Code 1.141.0 or the Copilot app 1.1.26; older clients are blocked when it's required.

macos.note: Copilot enforces its own sandbox; AgentEdict only sets it.

linux.note: Copilot enforces its own sandbox; AgentEdict only sets it.

windows.note: Copilot enforces its own sandbox; AgentEdict only sets it.

settings.title: Copilot: computer use
settings.description: Set to false to stop users turning on computer use in Copilot.

settings.title: Kiro: deny and ask rules
settings.description: Rules that deny or ask for Kiro's capabilities: file reads and writes, shell commands, web, MCP and more. Admin rules can't allow anything, and the stricter rule wins over the user's. A signin_method rule can deny sign-in methods (idc, external_idp, builder_id, google, github, social). At least one rule is required.

macos.note: Kiro must restart to pick up changes. Not yet checked on an installed client.

linux.note: Kiro must restart to pick up changes. Not yet checked on an installed client.

windows.note: Kiro must restart to pick up changes. Not yet checked on an installed client.

settings.title: Kiro: sign-in help link
settings.description: An https link shown to users when a sign-in method is blocked.

settings.title: Windsurf / Devin Desktop: allowed commands and MCP tools
settings.description: System hooks that block any terminal command or MCP tool that isn't listed exactly. Empty lists block all of them. MCP server labels are chosen by users, so they aren't a strong identity.

macos.note: Blocks only when the hook exits with code 2; a missing hook or Restricted Mode lets actions through.

linux.note: Blocks only when the hook exits with code 2; a missing hook or Restricted Mode lets actions through.

windows.note: Blocks only when the hook exits with code 2; a missing hook or Restricted Mode lets actions through.

settings.title: Cline: allowed tools and commands
settings.description: A Cline hook that cancels any tool not set to allow, and any command that isn't listed exactly. Each user must also run `edict install-hook cline`, and Cline lets actions through if the hook is missing or fails.

macos.note: Each user installs the hook and can remove it; Cline fails open.

linux.note: Each user installs the hook and can remove it; Cline fails open.

windows.note: Each user installs the hook and can remove it; Cline fails open.

settings.title: Managed agents
settings.description: The agents AgentEdict manages on each machine. Agents not listed are left alone.

settings.title: Standard policy
settings.description: The profile every managed agent gets when nobody logged in matches a rule for it. When several people are logged in, someone who matches no rule brings the standard at its priority, so it beats any rule numbered after it.

settings.title: Group rules
settings.description: Give users in certain groups a different profile. Each agent is matched on its own: a person gets their lowest-numbered matching rule for it, and across everyone logged in the lowest number wins. The builder numbers rules 10, 20, 30 in list order unless you type a number. Windows groups are written as a SID, entra:<object id>, .\LocalGroup or DOMAIN\Group.

settings.title: Blocked writes
settings.description: Paths the agent must never change. AgentEdict's profile format has this field, but it rejects a non-empty list today because no adapter can enforce it on its own. For Codex, use a permission profile with filesystem rules instead.

settings.title: Codex: sandbox rules per host
settings.description: Gives machines whose host name matches a pattern different allowed sandbox modes.

settings.title: Codex: allowed network domains
settings.description: A managed list of domains Codex's commands may reach. Codex marks it experimental.

macos.note: Experimental.

linux.note: Experimental.

settings.title: Codex: which apps computer use may control
settings.description: Rules for which apps Codex may operate through computer use. AgentEdict writes only allow_locked_computer_use today.

settings.title: Codex: allowed ChatGPT workspaces
settings.description: Lets users sign in only to approved ChatGPT workspaces. Only works from a local file.

settings.title: Codex: where sign-in credentials are kept
settings.description: Chooses where Codex stores sign-in credentials. Only works from a local file.

settings.title: Codex: ChatGPT service address
settings.description: Points Codex at a different ChatGPT service URL. Only works from a local file.

settings.title: Codex: approval reviewer policy
settings.description: Replaces the organization-specific part of the automatic reviewer's policy. OpenAI's page now documents this key; AgentEdict writes guardian_extra_policy instead, which needs checking against current Codex.

settings.title: Codex: managed hooks
settings.description: Lifecycle hooks the administrator installs for every Codex session.

settings.title: Codex: plugin marketplaces
settings.description: Limits where Codex plugins may come from.

settings.title: Codex: starting defaults
settings.description: Starting values, such as the sandbox mode and whether commands get network access. Users can change them during a session; requirements.toml is what limits them.

macos.note: Users can change these during a session.

linux.note: Users can change these during a session.

windows.note: In the user's own folder on Windows, so users can edit it.

settings.title: Codex: cloud-delivered requirements
settings.description: For users who sign in with ChatGPT Business or Enterprise, Codex can fetch the same requirements and defaults from OpenAI's admin console instead of a local file. Sign-in limits can't be set this way.

settings.title: Claude: starting permission mode
settings.description: Chooses the permission mode sessions start in, or removes auto mode.

settings.title: Claude: organization model limits
settings.vendor_key: claude.ai organization settings → model restrictions, default model, effort limits
settings.description: Turn models off, set the default model, and cap effort for the whole organization. Enforced by Anthropic's servers; doesn't reach Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry.

sources.title: Claude Code: set up for your organization

settings.title: Claude: spend and rate limits
settings.description: Spending and rate limits for the organization.

sources.title: Claude Code: set up for your organization

settings.title: OpenCode: allowed providers
settings.description: Only the listed providers load, or the listed ones never load. disabled_providers wins.

settings.title: OpenCode: default models
settings.description: The default model, and a smaller model for light tasks such as titles.

settings.title: OpenCode: automatic updates
settings.description: true, false, or "notify".

settings.title: OpenCode: turn tools on or off
settings.description: Turns individual tools on or off for the model.

settings.title: OpenCode: other permission rules
settings.description: Approval rules for tools other than shell commands and web fetch. AgentEdict always writes edit: allow.

settings.title: OpenCode: plugins
settings.description: npm plugins OpenCode loads.

settings.title: OpenCode: nested agents
settings.description: How many levels of helper agents may start other helpers (default 1).

settings.title: OpenCode: web server
settings.description: Settings for opencode serve and opencode web.

settings.title: Gemini: allowed tools list
settings.description: Only the listed tools are available, such as ReadFileTool or ShellTool(ls). Google recommends policy rules, which AgentEdict writes, over this list.

macos.note: The GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH variable can point Gemini at another settings file.

linux.note: The GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH variable can point Gemini at another settings file.

windows.note: The GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH variable can point Gemini at another settings file.

settings.title: Gemini: allowed MCP servers
settings.description: Lists the MCP servers users may run, and can deploy servers with only some of their tools exposed.

macos.note: Settings can be redirected by GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH.

linux.note: Settings can be redirected by GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH.

windows.note: Settings can be redirected by GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH.

settings.title: Gemini: required sign-in type
settings.description: Requires one sign-in method. Google moved unpaid and Google One users from Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI on 2026-06-18.

settings.title: Gemini: telemetry export
settings.description: Sends Gemini CLI telemetry to your collector. Google recommends logPrompts: false.

settings.title: Gemini: usage statistics
settings.description: Set to false to stop sending usage statistics to Google.

settings.title: Gemini: where /bug reports go
settings.description: Sends the /bug command to your own ticket system.

settings.title: Cursor: device policies
settings.vendor_key: AllowedExtensions, AllowedTeamId, ExtensionGalleryServiceUrl, NetworkDisableHttp2, UpdateMode, WorkspaceTrustEnabled
settings.description: Device policies for allowed extensions, which team may sign in, the extension marketplace, updates and Workspace Trust. Users can't override them.

linux.note: In the user's home folder on Linux.

settings.title: Cursor: auto-run allowlists
settings.description: Which terminal commands and MCP tools run without asking. The file sits in the user's home folder, so users can edit it, and project files add to it.

macos.note: Users can change it.

linux.note: Users can change it.

windows.note: Users can change it.

settings.title: Cursor: run mode and allowlists from the dashboard
settings.vendor_key: Team dashboard → Auto Run / Run Mode, MCP allowlist, sandbox network modes
settings.description: Admin allowlists and run mode set in Cursor's team dashboard. They replace the local file's lists and users can't override them.

settings.title: Cursor: enforce Privacy Mode
settings.description: Turns Privacy Mode on for everyone so members can't turn it off.

settings.title: Cursor: repository blocklist
settings.description: Repositories Cursor refuses to index or work with. Enterprise only.

settings.title: Cursor: model access
settings.vendor_key: Team dashboard → model and integration management
settings.description: Which models and integrations members may use.

settings.title: Antigravity: terminal auto-run
settings.vendor_key: Terminal command auto execution; terminal allowlist and denylist
settings.description: Whether terminal commands run without review, with allow and deny lists. Set by each user; Antigravity documents no admin-enforced version.

macos.note: Users can change it.

linux.note: Users can change it.

windows.note: Users can change it.

settings.title: Antigravity CLI: tool and review policy
settings.description: How the CLI asks before using tools (request-review, proceed-in-sandbox, strict, always-proceed) and reviews artifacts.

macos.note: Users can change it.

linux.note: Users can change it.

windows.note: Users can change it.

settings.title: Antigravity: files outside the workspace
settings.description: Whether the agent may touch files outside the open folder. Off by default.

macos.note: Users can change it.

linux.note: Users can change it.

windows.note: Users can change it.

settings.title: Antigravity: terminal sandbox
settings.vendor_key: enableTerminalSandbox (CLI); Enable Terminal Sandboxing, Sandbox Allow Network (IDE); Sandbox mode (App)
settings.description: Runs terminal commands in a sandbox, optionally with network access. Off by default.

macos.note: Users can change it.

linux.note: Users can change it.

windows.note: Users can change it.

settings.title: Antigravity: strict mode and browser rules
settings.vendor_key: Strict mode; browser JavaScript execution; browser URL allowlist and denylist
settings.description: Strict mode forces reviews and workspace isolation; the browser rules control scripts and which sites the agent may read.

macos.note: Users can change it.

linux.note: Users can change it.

windows.note: Users can change it.

settings.title: Antigravity: telemetry
settings.description: Whether interaction data is shared with Google.

macos.note: Users can change it.

linux.note: Users can change it.

windows.note: Users can change it.

settings.title: Copilot: default model
settings.description: The default model for new conversations, and the Auto routing tier.

settings.title: Copilot: plugins and marketplaces
settings.description: Turns plugins on or off and limits installs to listed marketplaces.

settings.title: Copilot: telemetry export
settings.description: Sends Copilot usage data to your OpenTelemetry collector.

settings.title: Copilot: remote control
settings.description: Limits remote control of sessions running on this device.

settings.title: Copilot: require fresh server settings
settings.description: Makes Copilot fetch server-managed settings at startup before running.

settings.title: Copilot: policies on github.com
settings.vendor_key: Enterprise or organization settings → Copilot policies (models, MCP registry, content exclusion, CLI access)
settings.description: Allowed models, MCP server policy, content exclusion and whether Copilot CLI may be used, set on github.com. Content exclusion doesn't apply to Copilot CLI.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot: supported surfaces for policies
Administer Copilot CLI for your enterprise

settings.title: Kiro: console governance
settings.vendor_key: Kiro console → governance: MCP, models, API keys, web tools
settings.description: Turns whole features on or off for the organization, such as MCP servers, models, API keys and web tools.

settings.title: Windsurf: terminal auto-run ceiling
settings.description: The highest auto-run level users may pick, from never to everything except a denylist. In beta.

settings.title: Windsurf: MCP and approved servers
settings.vendor_key: Admin Portal → MCP on/off and approved server list
settings.description: Turns MCP on or off and keeps the list of servers users may add.

settings.title: Windsurf: models
settings.description: Which models appear for users.

settings.title: Windsurf: feature switches
settings.vendor_key: Admin Portal → Web Search, MCP, Deploys
settings.description: Organization-wide switches for web search, MCP and deploys.

settings.title: Cline: remote configuration
settings.vendor_key: app.cline.bot → providers and models, MCP marketplace and servers, rules and workflows, telemetry, account switching
settings.description: Organization settings from Cline's hosted admin console. Only the VS Code and JetBrains extensions enforce them; the CLI and Cline Desktop don't. Cline documents its YOLO-mode switch as unsupported in every client.

macos.note: VS Code and JetBrains extensions only.

linux.note: VS Code and JetBrains extensions only.

windows.note: VS Code and JetBrains extensions only.
